Surah al-Hashr

Al-Mahayimi said: It was named so because the expulsion of the Jews is indicated in it, which shows God's kindness and care for His Messenger and the believers, and His subjugation and wrath against their enemies. This is among the greatest aims of the Qur'an.

Ibn 'Abbas used to say: It is the Surah of the Banu al-Nadir.

Al-Bukhari narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: I said to Ibn 'Abbas: "Surat al-Hashr?"

He said: "The Surah of the Banu al-Nadir."

And from him, he said: I said to Ibn 'Abbas: "Surat al-Hashr?" He said: "The Surah of the Banu al-Nadir." They were a people of the Jews. It is a Medinan surah, and its verses are twenty-four, without any disagreement.

(p-5734) In the name of God, the Compassionate, the Merciful.

On the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[1-2] "All that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth glorifies God, and He is the Mighty, the Wise. He it is who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Book from their homes at the first gathering. You did not think they would leave, and they thought that their fortresses would protect them from God; but God came upon them from where they had not expected, and cast terror into their hearts, so that they destroyed their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers. So take warning, O people of insight." [al-Hashr: 2]

"All that is in the heavens and all that is in the earth glorifies God, and He is the Mighty, the Wise": the interpretation of its counterpart has already been discussed. Then He pointed to an explanation of some effects of His might and the perfection of His wisdom, following His description with absolute compelling might and overwhelming wisdom, by His saying: "He it is who expelled those who disbelieved among the People of the Book" [al-Hashr: 2], meaning the Banu al-Nadir from among the Jews. "From their homes" [al-Hashr: 2], i.e., from their dwellings which they had made neighbours to the Muslims around Medina, out of kindness to them. "At the first gathering" [al-Hashr: 2], i.e., at the first assembling for fighting them. That is, God expelled them by His subjugation at the first time they were mustered for the raid against them. Specifying it by this is an indication of the severity of the Lord's seizing them and the strength of His might and retribution, by casting terror into their hearts, until they were compelled, at the first attack upon them, to exile and flight, as will come.

"You did not think they would leave" [al-Hashr: 2], i.e., because of the severity of their might and their strength. So it became a sign for you, because it is among the effects of God's sunnah, exalted is He, in humbling and subduing the corrupters. "And they thought that their fortresses would protect them from God" [al-Hashr: 2], i.e., from His might. "But God came upon them" [Al 'Imran: 148], i.e., His punishment, which was the terror and the compulsion to exile. "From where they had not expected" [al-Hashr: 2] (p-5735), i.e., they had not supposed it. "And He cast terror into their hearts" [al-Hashr: 2], i.e., He sent it down into them with great force, as the root of "qadhf" (casting) indicates, as if it were the hurling of stones.

Al-Qashani said: That is, He looked upon them with a glance of subjugation, and they were affected by it, because they deserved it, and because of their opposition, hostility and antagonism to the Beloved, and because of doubt in their hearts, and their being without insight into their affair and without clear proof from their Lord. For had they been people of certainty, terror would not have fallen into their hearts, and they would have recognised the Messenger of God (ﷺ) by the light of certainty, believed in him, and not opposed him.

"They destroy their houses with their own hands and the hands of the believers. So take warning, O people of insight" [al-Hashr: 2], i.e., see how what befell the corrupters befell them and what descended upon them descended, so that you may know the truth of God in His promise and His threat.

The Discussion Concerning the Interpretation of His Saying, Exalted Is He:

[3–4] ﴿And had it not been that Allah had decreed for them exile, He would have punished them in this world; and for them in the Hereafter is the punishment of the Fire.﴾ ﴿That is because they opposed Allah and His Messenger; and whoever opposes Allah – indeed, Allah is severe in penalty.﴾ [al-Hashr: 4]

﴿And had it not been that Allah had decreed for them exile﴾ – i.e., departure from their homelands – ﴿He would have punished them in this world﴾ – i.e., by killing and taking captive, as He did to their brethren, the Banu Qurayza.

**Commentary on the words of His saying, Exalted is He:**

[5] ﴿Whatever palm trees you cut down, or left standing on their roots, it was by the permission of God, and so that He might disgrace the defiant.﴾

﴿Whatever palm trees you cut down﴾, that is, a palm tree from among their palms, to enrage them. ﴿Or left standing on their roots﴾ (p-5736) ﴿it was by the permission of God﴾, that is, by His command and His approval, because that was not for mere sport or harm, but to strengthen the power of the truth, to fortify its people, and to terrify and humble the falsifiers, as God, Exalted is He, said: ﴿and so that He might disgrace the defiant﴾, that is, because of what it contains of humiliating the enemy, weakening him, and inflicting harm upon him.

**Note:**

The scholars of reports and the imams of biography (*siyar*) mention that the cause of the order to expel the Banu al-Nadir was their breach of the covenant. The Imam Ibn al-Qayyim said: When the Prophet (ﷺ) came to Medina, the disbelievers became three categories in relation to him. One category made a treaty with him and a truce, on condition that they would not fight him, would not back anyone against him, and would not ally with his enemy; they remained upon their disbelief, secure in their lives and property. A second category fought him and openly declared enmity against him. A third category abandoned him, neither making a treaty nor fighting him, but waited to see what his affair and the affair of his enemies would come to.

Among these, some loved his victory and triumph inwardly; others loved the victory of his enemy over him; and others entered with him outwardly while with his enemy inwardly, so as to be safe from both parties. These are the hypocrites.

He dealt with each of these groups according to what his Lord, Blessed and Exalted, had commanded him. He made a peace with the Jews of Medina and wrote between them a document of security. They were three tribes around Medina: the Banu Qaynuqa', the Banu al-Nadir, and the Banu Qurayza.

The Banu Qaynuqa' were the first to break what was between them and the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and they fought between Badr and Uhud. The Prophet (ﷺ) besieged them, then ordered them to leave Medina and not to fight him there. Then the Banu al-Nadir broke the covenant. That was because "the Messenger of God (ﷺ) went out to them seeking their help regarding the blood-money of two men from the Banu 'Amir, and the Messenger of God (ﷺ) sat beside a wall of their houses. They conspired to kill him (ﷺ), and that a man should climb up and drop a rock upon him. A man among them, 'Amr ibn Jihash ibn Ka'b, volunteered for this, and he climbed up to drop a rock on him. But revelation descended to the Messenger of God, upon whom be the blessings of God, concerning what the people intended. So he stood up and returned to Medina with those of his companions who were with him, and ordered preparation for war against them." Then he marched with the people until he came to them and besieged them for six nights, and they fortified themselves within their fortresses. "So the Messenger of God (ﷺ) ordered the palm trees to be cut down and burned." Then God cast terror into their hearts (p-5737), and they asked the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to expel them and spare their lives, on condition that they could take with them what their camels could carry of their property, except the armor. He agreed. They carried away of their property what their camels could bear; a man among them would tear down his house at the lintel of its door, place it on the back of his camel, and set off with it. They went out to Khaybar, and some of them went to Syria. They left the property to the Messenger of God (ﷺ), and it was his alone, to place wherever he wished. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) distributed it among the earlier emigrants (*muhajirun*) to the exclusion of the Helpers (*ansar*), except that Sahl ibn Hunayf and Abu Dujana mentioned their poverty, so the Messenger of God (ﷺ) gave to them. Only two men from the Banu al-Nadir became Muslim: Yamin ibn 'Umayr ibn Ka'b and Abu Sa'd ibn Wahb; they embraced Islam while keeping their property, and so they secured it."

Ibn Ishaq said: Some of the family of Yamin told me that "the Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to Yamin: 'Did you not see what I suffered from your cousin, and what they intended concerning me?' So Yamin ibn 'Umayr offered a man a reward on condition that he kill 'Amr ibn Jihash, and he killed him, as they claim." The entire Surah al-Hashr was revealed concerning the Banu al-Nadir, mentioning what God afflicted them with of His vengeance, what He empowered the Messenger of God (ﷺ) to inflict upon them, and what he did with them. End of quotation.

The discussion of the interpretation of His words, exalted is He:

[6] ﴿And whatever Allah restored to His Messenger from them—you did not spur over it horses or camels. But Allah gives His messengers power over whom He wills, and Allah is over all things competent.﴾

﴿And whatever Allah restored to His Messenger from them﴾ i.e., what He returned to him from the wealth of Banu al-Nadir. ﴿You did not spur over it horses or camels﴾ i.e., you did not drive horses or camels in obtaining it, nor did you pursue in the fighting for it; rather, you walked to it on your feet. The word (al-Ijaf) derives from (al-Wajif), which is the speed of travel, and (al-Rikab) is what is ridden of camels, the term being applied to it by the same token that the rider is named for the one he rides (i.e., the general term "rider" is used for the mount, by way of prominence).

(p-5738) ﴿But Allah gives His messengers power over whom He wills﴾ i.e., over the people of corruption and mischief, so that people may uphold justice. ﴿And Allah is over all things competent.﴾

Al-Zamakhshari said: The meaning is that what Allah granted His Messenger from the wealth of Banu al-Nadir is something they did not obtain through fighting and conquest; rather, Allah gave him power over them and over what was in their hands, just as He used to give His messengers power over their enemies. Therefore the matter concerning it is entrusted to him, and he places it wherever he wills. That is to say, it is not divided in the manner of the spoils of war, which were fought over and taken by force and compulsion. This is because they asked for a division, so the verse was revealed:

The Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on Surah 59, Verse 7:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[7] ﴿Whatever Allah has restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns — it belongs to Allah and to the Messenger and to the near relatives and the orphans and the needy and the traveler, so that it does not circulate solely among the rich from among you. And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it; and whatever he forbids you, abstain from it. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is severe in punishment.﴾

﴿Whatever Allah has restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns﴾ means: from the properties of their combatants. This is an explanation of the first [clause], and therefore it is not joined to it by a conjunction. ﴿it belongs to Allah and to the Messenger and to the near relatives and the orphans and the needy and the traveler, so that it does not﴾ — that is, the fay' whose right it is to belong to those mentioned — ﴿circulate solely among the rich from among you﴾, that is, they pass it around among themselves exclusively, apart from those who have a better right to it. Or [it means] a pre-Islamic circulation, since it was among their customs that the leaders and the wealthy monopolized the spoils to the exclusion of the poor. ﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you﴾ — that is, from the division of spoils or fay' — ﴿take it; and whatever he forbids you﴾ — that is, from taking it from them — ﴿abstain from it. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is severe in punishment﴾ — that is, for whoever opposes him in what he has forbidden.

(Notes)

The First: Al-Suyuti said in "al-Iklil": The verse has been cited as evidence that fay' is what is taken from the disbelievers without fighting, without the pressing of horses and camels, and among it is what they abandoned out of fear. And ghanima (spoils of war) is what is taken from them by fighting, as has preceded in His saying: ﴿And know that whatever you obtain of spoils﴾ [al-Anfal: 41], contrary to those who claim that the two have the same meaning, or who distinguish between them otherwise. End of quotation.

It seems that the one who claimed they have the same meaning saw that the general statement of this verse was clarified by the verse of al-Anfal, to the extent that Qatada claimed this verse is abrogated by that one. He said, as related from him by Ibn Jarir: The fay' was for these, then the Surah of al-Anfal abrogated that, saying:

﴿And know that whatever you obtain of spoils — indeed, for Allah is one-fifth of it, and for the Messenger, and for the near relatives and the orphans and the needy and the traveler﴾ [al-Anfal: 41]. And [in the Surah of al-Hashr] He made the one-fifth for those who were entitled to the fay'. The spoils used to be divided into five parts: four for the fighters, and one-fifth for the relatives of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) during his lifetime, one-fifth for the orphans, one-fifth for the needy, and one-fifth for the traveler.

The matter is expounded in the extended works of jurisprudence.

The Second: Al-Zamakhshari said: The better view is that His saying, exalted is He:

﴿And whatever the Messenger gives you, take it﴾ — the verse — is general over everything the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) brought and forbade. The matter of fay' falls within its generality.

In "al-Iklil": In it is the obligation to comply with his commands and prohibitions (ﷺ).

The scholars said: Everything that has been established from him (ﷺ) may be said to be in the Qur'an, taking this verse as the basis. End of quotation.

(p-5740) This last claim is an excess of the traditionalists (al-Athariyyun) and an overreach in deduction.

Then, exalted is He, specified from among the categories mentioned earlier those most deserving of care and attention, by His saying:

**On the interpretation (ta'wil) of His words, exalted is He:**

[8] ﴿For the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and their possessions, seeking bounty from Allah and His pleasure, and supporting Allah and His Messenger. Those are the truthful.﴾

﴿For the poor emigrants who were expelled from their homes and their possessions﴾, that is, from their homelands and the places they were familiar with. ﴿Seeking bounty from Allah﴾, that is, from knowledge and noble moral virtues. ﴿And pleasure﴾, that is, from Him, and this is the greatest thing to be desired. ﴿And supporting Allah and His Messenger﴾, that is, they give up their lives out of the strength of certainty (yaqin). ﴿Those are the truthful﴾. Al-Qashani said: that is, in their certain faith, so that their actions confirm their claim, since the sign of attaining certainty is the manifestation of its effect upon the limbs, such that their movements cannot occur except in accordance with what they witness of knowledge.

Then he pointed out that giving preference to these people in bestowal is something in which the hearts of their brothers, the Ansar, find contentment, because of their eagerness, may Allah be pleased with them, for preferring others over self-interest, by His saying:

The commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 59, verse 9:

Discussion of His words, exalted is He:

[9] ﴿And those who had already settled in the abode [of faith] and in belief before them love those who emigrate to them, and do not find in their breasts any need for what they have been given, and they prefer [them] over themselves, even though they themselves are in need. And whoever is protected from his own stinginess, it is those who are the successful.﴾

﴿And those who had already settled in the abode﴾, meaning the abode of emigration (hijrah), that is, they made it their home, ﴿and [in] belief before them﴾, meaning before the emigrants came to them. The word "belief" (al-iman) is said to be coordinated (ʿataf) with an implied verb: "and they held fast to belief (wa-akhlasū al-iman)". It was also said that the verb tabbaʾa (settle) was used in its necessary meaning, which is to remain and to establish oneself, so the meaning is: they remained in the abode and in belief. It was also permitted to treat belief as the place in which one settles, as a metaphor by implication (istiʿarah bi-l-kinayah), and settling is attributed to it by way of imagery (takhyil).

﴿They love those who emigrate to them﴾, meaning because of the shared kinship in purity of heart, agreement in religion, and brotherhood. Al-Shihab (al-Alusi) said: what is meant here by their love for the emigrants is their support for them, and their not finding it burdensome or resenting them when they are in need of them. So love is a metaphor for what has been mentioned, as is said:

*O my brother, and the wise person, if time betrays him, distinguishes the enemy from the one he loves.*

﴿And they do not find in their breasts﴾, meaning in their selves, ﴿any need﴾, meaning any desire or envy, ﴿for what they have been given﴾, meaning for what the emigrants were given of the spoils (fayʾ) and other things, due to the soundness of their hearts and their purity from the motives of greed.

﴿And they prefer [them] over themselves, even though they themselves are in need﴾, meaning they are in want and poverty.

Al-Qashani said: [this is] because of their detachment and their turning toward the presence of holiness, their elevation above the matters of impurity, and because excellence is for them an inherent matter, according to the demand of their nature, and the abundance of their love for brethren in truth and helpers in the path. So their giving precedence to their companions over themselves is due to the station of chivalry (futuwwah), the perfection of manliness, the strength of tawhid, and guarding against the portion of the self.

Note (tanbih):

In *al-Iklil*: the verse praises self-sacrifice (al-iʾthar) in matters of the self's portions and of worldly goods. End of quote.

Ibn Kathir said: this station is higher than the state of those whom God described in His words:

﴿And they give food, despite their love for it, to the needy, the orphan, and the captive﴾ [al-Insan: 8], and His words:

﴿and gives wealth, despite love for it﴾ [al-Baqarah: 177]. For those gave charity while they loved what they gave, and perhaps they had no need for it and no necessity for it. But these [i.e., the Ansar] preferred others over themselves despite their own want and need for what they spent. From this station is the charity of al-Siddiq (Abu Bakr), may God be pleased with him, with all his wealth. The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said to him: "What have you left for your family?" He said, may God be pleased with him: "I have left them God and His Messenger!" Likewise the water that was offered to Ikrimah and his companions on the day of al-Yarmuk: each of them ordered that it be given to his companion, while he was gravely wounded and in greatest need of water. Then the one [who had it] passed it to a third, but before it reached the third, they all died one after another, and none of them drank it. May God be pleased with them and make them content.

﴿And whoever is protected from his own stinginess﴾, meaning he opposes it in what dominates it of love of wealth and hatred of spending, ﴿it is those who are the successful﴾, meaning those who win both happinesses. Attributing stinginess (shuhh) to the self (nafs) is an indication of what al-Qashani said, that the self is the abode of every evil and defective quality, and the home of every impurity and base character. Stinginess is among its natural dispositions kneaded into its very clay, because it clings to the lower direction and loves partial portions. Therefore it is not removed from it except when the self itself is removed. But the one protected from those afflictions and evils is the one whom God protects.

Ibn Jarir said: In the language of the Arabs, shuhh means miserliness and withholding the surplus of wealth. The scholars hold that shuhh in this context is only consuming people's wealth unjustly. Then he related that a man came to Ibn Mas'ud and said: "O Abu Abd al-Rahman! I fear that this verse has afflicted me: ﴿And whoever is protected from his own stinginess, it is those who are the successful﴾, and I am a stingy man, nothing hardly ever leaves my hand!" He said: "That is not the stinginess that God mentioned in the Qur'an. Stinginess is that you consume your brother's wealth unjustly. That is miserliness, and miserliness is a wretched thing." End of quote.

It is apparent that by "the scholars" he meant those reported in that narration, because he explained it only by the transmitted report (al-ma'thur). Perhaps Ibn Mas'ud explained the verse this way because its context indicates it, since the aim is to discourage the Ansar from letting their souls aspire to what was given to the emigrants instead of them. Or he saw a distinction between shuhh and bukhl as he mentioned. In any case, the verse is not restricted to the interpretation he mentioned; rather, it is among what it admits.

From Ibn Zayd regarding the verse, he said: whoever is protected from his own stinginess, by not taking anything from the unlawful nor coming near it, and whom stinginess does not prevent from withholding anything of what is lawful, he is among the successful.

Ibn Jarir related from Anas ibn Malik who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Whoever pays zakat, hosts the guest, and gives in times of calamity, is free from stinginess."

Imam Ahmad related from Abdullah ibn Amr who said: The Messenger of God (ﷺ) said: "Beware of injustice, for injustice will be darkness on the Day of Resurrection. Beware of obscenity, for God does not love obscenity nor vulgarity. And beware of stinginess, for it destroyed those before you: it ordered them to injustice and they were unjust, it ordered them to wickedness and they were wicked, and it ordered them to sever ties and they severed them."

From Abu Hurayrah that he heard the Messenger of God (ﷺ) say: "Dust in the path of God and the smoke of Hell never gather in the belly of a servant, and stinginess and faith never gather in the heart of a servant."

The verse of Allah, the Exalted: [10]

﴿And those who came after them say: "Our Lord, forgive us and our brothers who preceded us in faith, and do not put in our hearts any resentment toward those who believe. Our Lord, You are Kind and Merciful."﴾

By "those who came after them" is meant those who emigrated after the strengthening of Islam, after the emigration of those who were driven out of their homes. So what is intended is their coming to Madinah after a period of time, and the coming is literal. It was also said: they are the believers after both groups until the Day of Resurrection, so the "coming" is either to existence or to faith. A parallel to this verse is the verse of Bara'ah:

﴿And the foremost early emigrants and the helpers and those who followed them with good conduct - Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him.﴾ [al-Tawbah: 100]

Al-Shihab said: What is meant by the supplication of the later for the earlier, and of the successor for the predecessor, is that they follow them, or it is an instruction to them to pray for those before them and to mention them with goodness.

Note:

al-Zamakhshari made his statement "and those who" (wa-alladhina) a conjunction upon "the emigrants" (al-muhajirin), like the relative pronoun before it in His saying: ﴿And those who had settled [in the city] before them﴾ [al-Hashr: 9], etc. Thus his statement "they love" (yuhibbuna) and his statement "they say" (yaqulun) would be two circumstantial clauses (hal). Al-Samin permitted a second possibility, namely that the relative pronoun in both is a subject (mubtada'), and what follows it is its predicate (khabar). In my view this is the correct position; what precedes it is strained, and the two relative clauses are resumed (mustani'af) to praise the faith of the Helpers and of those who follow them with those virtuous characteristics and perfect qualities. What led al-Zamakhshari and those who followed him to restrict themselves to the first possibility was only to include the categories of those who deserve the fay' (spoils gained without fighting) among the poor of each group, as if it were said: ﴿For the poor emigrants who were expelled﴾ [al-Hashr: 8], etc., "and for the poor who had settled [in the city]" etc., and for the poor who came after them... etc. Yet the context of the mentioned verses, and attention to the time of their revelation, when the emigrants were in hardship and the Helpers were in ease and plenty, indicate that what is intended by them concerning the fay' is specifically the poor of the emigrants. Those who had settled the abode had no need of it and no yearning for it, because of their great love for their brothers, and indeed their desire to give them preference. Then Allah, the Exalted, explained the condition of those who come after them: they praise those who preceded them and pray for them, delighted by what they did (p-5745) and pleased by what they did, because they are between one who emigrated away from his family and wealth out of love for Allah and His Messenger, and one who loves the one who emigrated, honors him, and indeed prefers him over himself. This reveals the strength of faith and the sincerity in strengthening the bonds of certainty. This is what is apparent from the arrangement of the noble verses and the taste of their flow. As for the poor of the other two groups, they deserve a share of the fay' by analogy with the first group, since they share in poverty. However, in the time of the Prophet (ﷺ), none of the Helpers complained of poverty in that event, except Sahl and Abu Dujanah, as has preceded, and he (ﷺ) gave to them both. As for other events in which the spoils were abundant, their share of them was what is known and clarified in other verses, for the noble revelation explained the distribution of wealth to its owners in several verses.

Ibn Jarir narrated that Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) recited: ﴿Charity is only for the poor and the needy﴾ [al-Tawbah: 60] until he reached: ﴿All-Knowing, All-Wise﴾ [al-Tawbah: 60]. Then he said: "This is for those." Then he recited: ﴿And know that whatever you obtain of war booty, a fifth of it is for Allah and for the Messenger﴾ [al-Anfal: 41], the verse. Then he said: "This verse is for those." Then he recited: ﴿What Allah has restored to His Messenger from the people of the towns﴾ [al-Hashr: 7] until he reached: ﴿And those who came after them﴾. Then he said: "This verse has encompassed the Muslims in general, so there is no one except that he has a right in it. If I live, the shepherd will surely come, while he is driving his donkeys, [to receive] his share, and his brow will not have been moistened with sweat over it."

The discussion of the Almighty's saying:

[11] ﴿Have you not seen those who played the hypocrite say to their brothers who disbelieve among the People of the Book, "If you are expelled, we will surely leave with you, and we will never obey anyone concerning you, and if you are fought, we will surely support you." And Allah testifies that they are liars.﴾

(p-5746) ﴿Have you not seen those who played the hypocrite say to their brothers who disbelieve among the People of the Book﴾ meaning the Banu al-Nadir, who were mentioned earlier. Their "brotherhood" with them was a brotherhood of religion and belief, or a brotherhood of friendship and alliance, because they were secretly with them against the believers. ﴿"If you are expelled"﴾ i.e., from your homes, ﴿"we will surely leave with you, and we will never obey anyone concerning you"﴾ i.e., in forsaking you, ﴿"anyone ever"﴾ i.e., from the Messenger, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, and the believers. ﴿"And if you are fought, we will surely support you"﴾ i.e., we will surely aid you.

Ibn Jarir said: It has been mentioned that those who played the hypocrite were Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, Wadi'ah and Malik, the two sons of Nawfal, Suwayd, and DA'is. They sent to the Banu al-Nadir when the Messenger of Allah ﷺ came against them for war, saying: "Stand firm and defend yourselves; for we will not hand you over, and we are with you. If you are fought, we will fight; and if you are expelled, we will leave with you." So they waited for their support, but they did not act, and Allah cast terror into their hearts, so they asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to exile them and to spare their lives, on condition that they may take with them whatever their camels could carry of their property, except the armor, as was mentioned earlier. ﴿"And Allah testifies that they are liars"﴾ i.e., because He knows that they will not do that, as He said:

The discussion of the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[12] ﴿If they are expelled, they will not go out with them; and if they are fought, they will not help them; and if they help them, they will surely turn their backs; then they will not be helped.﴾

﴿If they are expelled, they will not go out with them; and if they are fought, they will not help them; and if they help them, they will surely turn their backs⁠

The discussion on the interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[13] ﴿Indeed, you are more fearsome in their breasts than Allah. That is because they are a people who do not comprehend.﴾

﴿Indeed, you are more fearsome in their breasts than Allah. That is because they are a people who do not comprehend.﴾ That is: (p-5747) they fear you more than they fear Allah, because they are veiled by creation from the Truth, due to their ignorance of Allah and their failure to know Him. For had they known Him, they would have felt His greatness, His power and His knowledge, and they would not have treated His acts of disobedience lightly or treated His commands lightly. The pronoun [in "their breasts" and "they"] refers to the hypocrites or the Jews.

**The discourse on the interpretation (ta'wil) of His saying, may He be exalted:**

[14] ﴿They will not fight you all together, except in fortified villages or from behind walls. Their violence among themselves is severe. You think them united, but their hearts are divided. That is because they are a people who do not understand.﴾

﴿They will not fight you﴾, i.e., the Jews and their allies, ﴿all together, except in fortified villages﴾, i.e., with fortresses, so they do not come out to open combat, ﴿or from behind walls﴾, i.e., from behind barriers, because of their extreme fear of you.

﴿Their violence among themselves is severe﴾. Al-Zamakhshari said: He means that the severe violence for which they are described exists only among themselves when they fight one another. Had they fought you, that violence and severity would not remain for them, because the brave become cowardly and the mighty become humbled when they confront God and His Messenger. End of quotation.

﴿You think them united, but their hearts are divided﴾, i.e., you suppose them gathered together because of their outward agreement, while their hearts are scattered, due to the difference of their aims, the pull of their motives, and their divergence from the truth into falsehood.

﴿That﴾. Al-Mahayimi said: i.e., the outward gathering together alongside the inward division. ﴿That is because they are a people who do not understand﴾, i.e., this causes their cowardice, which leads to total destruction. End of quotation.

In these three verses there is encouragement for the believers to confront them, to press upon them, and good news for them that they will be the victorious and dominant ones.

Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 59, verse 15:

The interpretation of His saying, exalted is He:

[15] ﴿Like those before them, who had recently tasted the evil consequence of their affair; and for them is a painful punishment.﴾

﴿Like those before them, who had recently tasted the evil consequence of their affair; and for them is a painful punishment.﴾ That is: (p-5748) like these Jews of Banu al-Nadir, in what befell them of punishment, like the example of those who received the requital of their transgression before them, namely the disbelievers of Quraysh at the Battle of Badr, or Banu Qaynuqa'. Ibn Kathir said: The second is closer to the truth, for the Jews of Banu Qaynuqa' had been expelled by the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) before this. End of quote.

Qatadah said: Banu Qaynuqa' were the first Jews to break what was between them and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and they fought between Badr and Uhud. The matter concerning them was that a woman from the Arabs came with some goods of hers and sold them in the market of Banu Qaynuqa', and sat down beside a goldsmith there. They began to urge her to uncover her face, but she refused. So the goldsmith went to the edge of her garment and tied it to her back, and when she stood up, her private parts were exposed, so they laughed at her. She cried out, and a man from the Muslims leapt upon the goldsmith and killed him, and he was a Jew. The Jews then attacked the Muslim and killed him, and the family of the Muslim called upon the Muslims for help against the Jews. The Muslims became angry, and evil broke out between them and Banu Qaynuqa'. "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) besieged them until they came down to his judgment, and he commanded them to leave Madinah and not to live as neighbours to him therein," so they went out to Syria. The details are in the books of biography (sirah).

Ibn Jarir said: The most correct of the opinions is to say: Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, made these disbelievers among the People of the Book, from what He is causing them to taste of His punishment, an example by those before them of those who denied His Messenger (ﷺ), whom He destroyed in His wrath. The matter of Banu Qaynuqa' and the Battle of Badr were both before the expulsion of Banu al-Nadir, and all of those have tasted the evil consequence of His command. Allah, Mighty and Majestic is He, did not single out some of them in the illustration of these people by them to the exclusion of others. Every one of them tasted the evil consequence of his affair, so whoever's time was near to theirs, they are made an example by them in that for which the example was intended. End of quote.

(p-5749)

The Discussion on the Interpretation of His, the Exalted, Words:

[16–17] ﴿Like the Shaytan (Satan) when he says to man, "Disbelieve." But when he disbelieves, he says, "Indeed, I am free of you; indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds."﴾ ﴿So the end of both of them will be that they are in the Fire, abiding eternally therein. And that is the recompense of the wrongdoers.﴾ [al-Hashr: 17]

﴿Like the Shaytan﴾ means: like the hypocrites in their incitement of the Banu al-Nadir to fight, and their promise to them of support or of going out with them, and like the Banu al-Nadir's being deceived by those people's false promise. It is like the Shaytan ﴿when he says to man, "Disbelieve"﴾, meaning: when he deceives a man and promises him, in return for following him and disbelieving in Allah, support at the time of need for him. ﴿But when he disbelieves﴾, meaning: in Allah, and follows and obeys him. ﴿He says﴾, meaning: out of fear that he will share with him in his punishment, submitting to him and forsaking him: ﴿"Indeed, I am free of you"﴾, meaning: so I will not help you. ﴿"Indeed, I fear Allah, Lord of the worlds"﴾, meaning: regarding your support. And that is the recompense of the wrongdoers﴾ [al-Hashr: 17], meaning: with regard to the right of Allah, the Exalted, and the rights of the servants. That is, thus is the recompense of the Jews of the Banu al-Nadir and of the hypocrites who promised them support. Each one who disbelieves in Allah is a wrongdoer to himself by his disbelief in Him. Indeed, they are in the Fire, abiding eternally.

The commentary on the words of Allah, the Exalted:

[18] ﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah. And let every soul look to what it has put forward for tomorrow. And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾

﴿O you who have believed, fear Allah﴾ means: by performing His obligations and avoiding His prohibitions.

Al-Mahayimi said: That is, the requirement of your faith is that you not feel secure from the plotting of Allah. So fear Him, lest He give Satan power over you to lead you astray into disbelief, and then Satan disowns you.

﴿And let every soul look to what it has put forward for tomorrow﴾ means: for what comes after death of righteous deeds. ﴿And fear Allah; indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what you do﴾ means: He will reward you according to them.

(p-5750)

The explanation of His words, Exalted is He:

[19] ﴿And be not like those who forgot Allah, so He caused them to forget themselves. Those are the defiantly disobedient.﴾

﴿And be not like those who forgot Allah, so He caused them to forget themselves﴾. Ibn Jarir said: That is, do not be like those who neglected to fulfill the right of Allah that He made obligatory upon them, so He caused them to forget their own share of good things.

Al-Qashani said:

﴿Forgot Allah﴾, that is, by veiling themselves through bodily desires and occupation with the pleasures of the soul. ﴿So He caused them to forget themselves﴾, until they regarded themselves as the body, its composition and its temperament, and so they were distracted from the holy essence and the luminous natural disposition.

Ibn al-Qayyim said in *Dar al-Sa'adah*: Reflect on this verse and you will find beneath it a noble and great meaning, which is that whoever forgets his Lord, Allah causes him to forget his own self and soul, so he does not know its reality or its interests. Rather, he forgets what its well-being and success depend upon, in his life in this world and in the Hereafter. Thus he becomes neglected and left aside, in the position of free-roaming livestock. Indeed, perhaps the livestock are more knowledgeable of their interests than he is, because they remain upon the guidance that their Creator gave them. As for this person, he has departed from the natural disposition upon which he was created. So he forgot his Lord, and Allah caused him to forget his own self, its attributes, what it is perfected by, what it is purified by, and what it is made happy by in its life and its return. Allah, Exalted is He, said:

﴿And do not obey one whose heart We have made heedless of Our remembrance, who follows his own desire and whose affair has become neglect.﴾ [Al-Kahf: 28]

So he became heedless of the remembrance of his Lord, and his affair and his heart were lost to him. He pays no attention to his interests, his perfection, or what purifies his soul and heart. Rather, he is scattered in heart, wasted, his affair is neglected, and he is bewildered, not finding the way. Knowledge of Allah is the root of all knowledge, and it is the root of the servant's knowledge of his happiness and perfection, and the interests of his worldly life and his Hereafter. Ignorance of Him necessarily entails ignorance of his own self, its interests, its perfection, and what it is purified and made successful by. So knowledge of Him is the servant's happiness, and ignorance of Him is the root of his wretchedness. End of quotation.

(p-٥٧٥١) ﴿Those are the defiantly disobedient﴾, that is, those who departed from the upright religion, which is the natural disposition of Allah upon which He created mankind. They betrayed and were treacherous, and they cast the covenant of Allah behind their backs, and so they lost.

The discussion concerning His words, may He be exalted:

[20] ﴿The companions of the Fire and the companions of Paradise are not equal. The companions of Paradise are the ones who are the triumphant.﴾

﴿The companions of the Fire are not equal﴾ — and they are the forgetful, the treacherous — ﴿and the companions of Paradise﴾ — and they are the believers, the God-fearing, those who fulfil their covenant.

﴿The companions of Paradise are the ones who are the triumphant﴾ — that is, with everlasting bliss.

Two notes:

The first: al-Zamakhshari said: The companions of al-Shafi'i, may Allah be pleased with him, cited this verse as evidence that a Muslim is not to be killed for a disbelieving dhimmi. End of quote.

One of the imams of the Shafi'is, Burhan al-Din, in his work "Tafdil al-Salaf 'ala al-Khalaf," rejected this use of the verse with words to the following effect:

Some of the Shafi'is argued with this verse in the question of killing a Muslim for a dhimmi, and this is extremely weak, because no one has equated the two. Imposing retaliation (qisas) is not equality, for there is no pair of things that differ in some respects that do not also agree in some respect or respects; therefore imposing retaliation is not equality, just as imposing blood-money (diyya) and expiation (kaffara) is not equality. This statement reflects weakness of judgment in the matter of deriving inference from the evidences of the Furqan. End of quote.

The second: Abu al-Su'ud said: Perhaps the mention of the companions of the Fire first is to indicate from the outset that the deficiency which the non-equality reveals is on their part, not on the part of their counterparts. For the concept of non-equality between two things that differ in excess and deficiency, although it may be considered in terms of the excess of the one that exceeds, the more immediate sense is to consider it in terms of the deficiency of the one that is deficient. Upon this is His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Are the blind and the seeing equal, or are the darknesses and the light equal?﴾ [al-Ra'd: 16], and other such instances. As for His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿Are those who know and those who do not know equal?﴾ [al-Zumar: 9], perhaps the mention of the superior first there is because its attribute is a settled quality (malaka) relative to the attribute of the inferior, and privations are preceded by the qualities they negate. End of quote.

The Interpretation of His Words, exalted is He:

[21] ﴿Had We sent down this Qur'an upon a mountain, you would have seen it humbled, split asunder out of fear of God. And these are the parables We set forth for people, that perhaps they might reflect.﴾

﴿Had We sent down this Qur'an﴾, that is: the one that gathers the admonitions, which necessitates reflection and God-consciousness in every state, ﴿upon a mountain﴾. Al-Mahayimi said: that is, by making it comprehend it and charging it with what is in it, after giving it the faculties of perception and motion. ﴿You would have seen it humbled﴾, that is: abased before the greatness of God, ﴿split asunder﴾, that is: cracked, ﴿out of fear of God﴾, that is: despite its great magnitude, the extremity of its hardness, and the utmost of its firmness. Al-Qashani said: that is, their hearts are harder than stone in not being affected and not accepting, since the Divine speech has reached such a degree of influence that no greater increase is possible beyond it, so that even if it were supposed to be sent down upon a mountain, it would be affected by it with humility and splitting. ﴿And these are the parables We set forth for people﴾, that is: and these matters, although they are imaginary and supposed, must be considered and set forth for the people who have forgotten their own smallness and so became arrogant, and whose hearts were hardened after being softened. ﴿That perhaps they might reflect﴾, that is: so that they may know that He is more worthy of that humility and splitting.

Al-Zamakhshari said: the verse is an illustration (tamthil), as was mentioned in His words: ﴿Indeed, We offered the trust﴾ [al-Ahzab: 72], and what indicates this is His words: ﴿And these are the parables We set forth for people﴾. The purpose is to rebuke the human being for the hardness of his heart and the scarcity of his humility when contemplating the Qur'an and contemplating its impactful and admonishing warnings.

Then the Exalted indicated how humility could be abandoned toward the Essence of God and His Names, when He is:

(p-5753)

**Commentary on His saying, Exalted is He:**

**[22–24]** ﴿He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, Knower of the unseen and the witnessed. He is the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful.﴾ ﴿He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, the King, the Pure, the Source of Peace, the Granter of Security, the Guardian, the Mighty, the Compeller, the Supreme. Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him.﴾ [59:23] ﴿He is Allah, the Creator, the Originator, the Fashioner. To Him belong the most beautiful names. Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him, and He is the Mighty, the Wise.﴾ [59:24]

﴿He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity﴾, i.e., the one worshipped, to whom alone worship and divinity are fitting. ﴿Knower of the unseen and the witnessed﴾, i.e., what is hidden from the senses and what is perceived. ﴿He is the Most Merciful, the Especially Merciful﴾, i.e., the Bestower of general and particular blessings. Whoever is aware of secrets loves to humble himself before Him and to fear Him, especially in respect of His being a bestower of blessings, for it is the right of the bestower that one humble oneself before Him and fear that his blessings may be taken away.

﴿He is Allah, other than whom there is no deity, the King﴾ [59:23], i.e., the absolutely Self-Sufficient, whom everything needs, the Administrator of all things in an arrangement that admits no perfection beyond it. ﴿The Pure﴾ [59:23], i.e., the One far exalted above whatever is unfitting to His majesty, with the utmost exaltation. ﴿The Source of Peace﴾ [59:23], i.e., the One from whose injustice His creatures are safe, or the One free from deficiencies such as incapacity. ﴿The Granter of Security﴾ [59:23], i.e., to the people of certainty by sending down tranquility and by protecting from the terror of the Hereafter. ﴿The Guardian﴾ [59:23], i.e., the Watcher over everything by His knowledge, His dominion and His preservation. ﴿The Mighty﴾ [59:23], i.e., the Strong, who overcomes and is not overcome. ﴿The Compeller﴾ [59:23], i.e., the One whose will takes effect by way of compulsion over every person, while no one's will can take effect against Him, and from whose grip no one escapes. This was stated by al-Ghazali in *al-Maqsad al-Asna*.

Imam Ibn al-Qayyim said in *al-Kafiya al-Shafiya*:

*And likewise al-Jabbar is among His attributes, and compulsion within His attributes is of two kinds:*
*The mending of the weak and of every heart that has become broken, and mending from Him is near.*
*And the second is the compulsion of dominion through the might that is not fitting for anyone other than Him among mankind.*
*And He has a third name, which is the Most High, so no one among mankind draws near to Him,*
*From the saying of the people, "a tall date palm" (jabbarah) for the lofty palm tree that escapes every finger.*

﴿The Supreme﴾ [59:23], i.e., the One who sees everything as insignificant in comparison to His own essence, and who sees greatness and majesty only as belonging to Himself, so He regards others as kings regard slaves. ﴿Exalted is Allah above what they associate with Him﴾ [59:23], i.e., above the idols and the intercessors.

﴿He is Allah, the Creator﴾ [59:24], i.e., the One who determines things in accordance with the requirements of His wisdom. ﴿The Originator﴾ [59:24], i.e., the One who brings them into existence after non-existence. ﴿The Fashioner﴾ [59:24], i.e., of beings, as He wills.

﴿To Him belong the most beautiful names﴾ [59:24], i.e., those that indicate excellent meanings and the finest praises.

﴿Whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him, and He is the Mighty, the Wise﴾ [59:24], i.e., in His management of His creation and in directing them to what contains their welfare and happiness.

**Remarks:**

**First:** Al-Sayyid Ibn al-Murtada said in *Ithar al-Haqq*: The station of knowing the perfection of the Generous Lord, and what is due to Him of His attributes and His most beautiful names, is part of the complete *tawhid* (affirmation of God's oneness) which is indispensable, because the perfection of the essence is through His most beautiful names and their noble attributes, and there is no perfection for an essence that has neither attribute nor name. For this reason, the doctrine of the atheists, who praise the Lord by negating them, is regarded as among their greatest stratagems against Islam, for they reversed what is known by reason and by revelation. They censured the praiseworthy matter and praised the blameworthy matter, which stands in place of negation and pure denial, and they opposed the Book of Allah and its clear texts. Allah, Majestic is His majesty, said:

﴿To Allah belong the most beautiful names, so call upon Him by them, and leave those who deviate concerning His names﴾ [7:180]. And He, Glorified and Exalted, said: ﴿Say: Call upon Allah or call upon the Most Merciful; whichever you call, to Him belong the most beautiful names﴾ [17:110].

So whatever among them is stated in the Book of Allah must be believed in by all, and whoever denies it, or claims that its apparent meaning is a name of blame for Allah, Glorified is He, must be rebuked. Whatever is found in a *hadith* (prophetic report) must be believed by one who knows its authenticity. Whatever falls below this level, or whose authenticity is disputed, may not be used, for Allah is too exalted to be named by a name whose use by Himself has not been established.

Then he said: It is the custom of some scholars of hadith to list all that has been reported in the well-known hadith concerning their enumeration, despite the famous disagreement about its authenticity. It is enough for you that al-Bukhari and Muslim both left its transmission, along with the transmission of its beginning, and their agreement on this indicates the strength of its defect. However, most scholars relied upon it, seeking the great grace of Allah in His promise to whoever enumerates them that he will enter Paradise, as its authenticity is agreed upon. Their enumeration can be certain in this manner only if Allah, Glorified is He, had no name other than those names. But since His names, Glorified is He, are more than can be counted, the certainty of that is void, and it is better to limit oneself to what is in the Book of Allah and to what is agreed upon as authentic after that, which is rare. It has been established by necessity and by explicit text that the names of Allah, Exalted is He, are more than that which has been transmitted.

Then he, may Allah have mercy on him, extended and excelled in this matter. Let the one who seeks thorough verification refer to it.

**Second:** Al-Ghazali said in *al-Maqsad al-Asna*, which is among the most valuable works composed on the meanings of the most beautiful names: Do the attributes and the names applied to Allah, Exalted is He, depend on divine stipulation (*tawqif*), or are they permissible by way of reason? What al-Qadi Abu Bakr al-Baqillani inclined to is that this is permissible, except what the Shariah prohibits or what indicates something whose meaning is impossible for Allah, Exalted is He.
